html:
The First Punic War was fought from 264 to 241 BCE between Rome and Carthage, the two great powers of the western Mediterranean. It lasted 23 years, mostly on and around Sicily, and was the largest naval war of the ancient world.

It began over Messana, on the strait between Sicily and Italy, whose mercenary rulers asked both powers for help. Rome crossed to Sicily and soon won over Hiero II of Syracuse.

  • Rome had almost no navy. It built fleets of warships, reportedly copying a wrecked Carthaginian ship, and fitted them with a boarding bridge, the corvus, so that sea battles became land battles. It won at Mylae in 260 BCE.
  • A Roman invasion of Africa under Regulus was crushed in 255 BCE.
  • Storms sank whole Roman fleets, and Carthage won at sea at Drepana in 249 BCE. Hamilcar Barca held out in western Sicily for years.
  • A last Roman fleet, paid for by rich citizens, won off the Aegates Islands in 241 BCE.

Carthage gave up Sicily, which became Rome's first province, and paid a large indemnity. The resentment led on to the Second Punic War. Our main source is Polybius.
